claims: Hail is solid precipitation consisting of ice lumps.
Hail is formed when thunderstorm updrafts carry water droplets into extremely cold upper atmosphere, freezing them.
Hailstones grow through repeated lifting and accretion.
Hailstones fall at speeds up to 100+ mph.
Hail is formed in warm-season thunderstorms via strong updrafts.
Sleet occurs in cold weather, usually during winter.
Sleet does not grow in storms.
A record-contending 6+ inch diameter hailstone was reported in Illinois on March 10, 2026.
The official largest recorded hailstone in the US was 4.75 inches in 2015.
Nebraska, Colorado, and Wyoming experience the most hailstorms, according to the NSSL.
Severe hail causes nearly one billion dollars in property and crop damage annually, notes the NWS.
